evidence: No tool lists the 3D-ΔPDF's strongest features with their vectors and signs, which the task and delta-pdf-interpretation step 3 ask for: dpdf_contrast reports the strongest feature in σ without its place, measure_dpdf_cut an SNR and an anisotropy, and line_profile reads a line the model must already have chosen.
proposed_fix: A dpdf_peaks tool: the extrema of the ΔPDF above a few robust σ outside the origin's disk, each with its vector in Å and r.l.u., its sign and its size in σ, read from the 3D volume on the server.
note: dpdf_peaks, default 5σ and 12 entries. On the dev control the planted ⟨3/2 0 0⟩+ is entry 7 (238σ) and the weaker ⟨½ 1 1⟩− entry 19 (73σ): a model asks for up to 30.

evidence: ub_check reads the shifted origin (planted at (0.03, 0.02, 0) r.l.u.) as an offset RMS of 0.0583 Å⁻¹ that the fit leaves at 0.0583, and says to look at the origin. No tool gives the shift itself, so a report on the origin can name no size.
proposed_fix: Report the mean offset of the node centres from their nodes in r.l.u. (a vector, before and after the fit) in ub_check's result.
note: mean_offset_rlu before and after the fit; origin_shift_rlu when the offsets are unexplained and that vector makes 0.8 or more of the RMS the fit leaves. Dev origin case: (0.0305, 0.0195, 0) for (0.03, 0.02, 0).

evidence: assess_stage fails the ΔPDF below a back-FFT r of 0.999. On the clean control r is 0.989 (0.989 to 0.996 on all eight dev cases) and the normalised RMS 0.125. The transform keeps the real part, the part of the data even under Q → −Q, so on unsymmetrised noisy data r measures the noise in the odd part: the same volume averaged with its inversion gives r = 1.0, RMS 0.
proposed_fix: Compare the round trip with the data's Q → −Q even part, or judge r only on volumes declared symmetrised.
tests: web/src/llm/__tests__/evaluate.test.ts (judges the round trip against the data's even part)
note: Both options of the fix: r is judged against the data's Q → −Q even part (pearson_r_even, 1 on all eight dev cases), and a check recorded before that comparison judges r against the data only on data the file declares symmetrised.

evidence: texture_check flags a systematic fill bias on all three cuts of the clean control: median fill 0.65, 0.57 and 1.34 rim σ, 88 to 96 % of the holes above their rim. The bias is in rim σ, which shrinks with the counts, with no floor in units of the diffuse level, and the demo's diffuse peaks at every node (TDS), so a fill above its rim is expected.
proposed_fix: Give the bias a floor in units of the local diffuse level, and compare the fill with what an interpolation of a node-peaked diffuse gives, not with the rim's median.
note: The reference is the range from the measured rim's flat to its linear (node-peaked) continuation; the floor is a fifth of the local diffuse level (FILL_BIAS_FLOOR), provisional. No dev cut is flagged.

evidence: reduction-qc step 6 says a rising floor wants the Q² term but not when to turn it on. assess_stage now states pedestal_left (true on this case, trend 0.84 and span 0.84; false after the term: trend 0.29). The term is not free where there is no such background: on the clean controls it raised the scored pedestal span from 0.025 to 0.066 to 0.107.
proposed_fix: Add to step 6: turn flattenQ2 on when assess_stage for the flatten reports pedestal_left, rerun, and read it again; leave it off otherwise.
tests: web/src/llm/__tests__/skills.test.ts (says when the flatten's Q² term goes on; on validation/batch-1-skills)
note: Skill text, in its own PR (validation/batch-1-skills), which waits for the user's review; the skill stays a draft awaiting the user's interview. That PR also holds the skill lines findings 1, 3 and 4 touch (delta-pdf-interpretation steps 2–3 and check 4, bragg-node-audit step 7).

evidence: The flatten verdict is "needs attention" on all eight dev volumes, the clean control and the planted case after the Q² term included, because the floors read 1.5 to 1.8 σ against the limit of 1σ (control 1.72σ, trend 0.52, span 1.24). The clause cannot be met on these volumes whatever the flatten did; the pedestal rule separates them.
proposed_fix: The user's call: keep the 1σ clause, widen it, or drop it where the floors follow the diffuse level.
tests: web/src/llm/__tests__/report.test.ts (judges the flatten by the pedestal rule)
note: Approved by the user on 2026-10-17, option "drop": the 1σ clause is dropped from the flatten's verdict, which rests on the pedestal rule (a trend and a span both 0.8 or more of the diffuse level); the floor in σ is still reported. Labelled provisional in the code and docs, as the 0.8 limits are.

evidence: The counts end at 4.507 Å⁻¹ (put in at 4.511) of a box whose nearest face is 6.44 Å⁻¹, and qmax_coverage opens "clean: … 9.8e-4 of its weight on unmeasured reciprocal space", just under the 1e-3 limit. The counts' edge and the band 0 to 4.5 are in raw_counts and suggested_band, not in the verdict a model quotes.
proposed_fix: When the counts end inside the box and no band is set, say so in the verdict or band_check, with the edge and the suggested band.
tests: web/src/llm/__tests__/tools.test.ts (qmax_coverage: says in the verdict when the counts end inside the box)
note: The verdict and band_check give the edge, the box face and the band when the counts end at least 0.1 Å⁻¹ inside the nearest face and no band is set.

evidence: The flatten reads a falling floor on the cut-coverage case (trend −0.82, span 1.19) and so pedestal_left, where the planted truth has no pedestal (the default run's pedestal span is 0.015 of the diffuse level, against the 0.25 limit). floor_before is empty there.
proposed_fix: Judge the pedestal over the shells the counts reach only, and find why the floors fall on a cut volume.
tests: web/src/llm/__tests__/evaluate.test.ts (says whether the flatten left a pedestal)
note: Why the floors fall: they follow the crystal's own diffuse level (a hump at 1.7 Å⁻¹ and its fall), which the full control reads the same over the same shells. The trend and span are now judged over the outer half of the fully measured shells; provisional, as the 0.8 limits are.
